prerequisites: Knowledge of mathematics in the field of: vector analysis, differential and integral calculus

learning_outcomes.text: Knows and understands basic concepts of vector analysis and differential calculus
Possesses knowledge about basic mathematical dependencies in electromagnetic field theory
Knows, understands, and can interpret the equations of electrodynamics (Maxwell's equations)
Knows and understands phenomena accompanying the propagation of low-frequency electromagnetic waves
Can logically link the laws governing the electromagnetic field (stationary and non-stationary)
Can solve basic field boundary problems using one of the learned methods
Can determine electrical (capacitance) and magnetic (inductance) parameters of exemplary electrical objects
Can determine basic parameters of a low-frequency electromagnetic wave
Understands the need and knows the possibilities of continuous self-education and raising professional competencies

syllabus_topics: Principles of credit and historical overview. Mathematical apparatus: review of vector calculus, basic mathematical dependencies concerning the electromagnetic field and their physical interpretation.
Maxwell's laws and their interpretation. Properties of the electrostatic field.
Basic laws and properties of the flow field.
Application of field theory to calculate temperature distributions. Dependencies describing the magnetic field.
Electromagnetic induction phenomenon - Faraday's law. Influence of frequency on the classification of environments subjected to harmonic field interaction.
Electromagnetic field propagation. Plane wave in dielectric and conductor.
Analytical and numerical methods for field determination, introduction to computer calculations.
teaching_methods: Practice method (doing tasks at the blackboard)

assessment_methods.method: Auditorium classes Test (quizzes and oral answers)

assessment_rules: The form of the lecture examination will be determined at the first lecture, depending on the number of students. Auditorium classes are credited based on quiz results and oral answers. The instructor may also propose simple computational projects for willing students. The student's work assessment may be based on oral or written statements in the form of a colloquium, which, in accordance with the AGH study regulations, translates into the final grade for this form of classes.
